name: console-run-command
title: Run Console Command

description: Run Python inside the Unreal Editor (PythonScriptPlugin, full `unreal` API, pre-imported). Write plain statements; the LAST EXPRESSION is the result (objects come back as their paths). print() and unreal.log*() output is returned as logs; errors point at snippet.py lines. Each call starts from a fresh namespace. Its recorded edits are one undo step (so the snippet itself cannot run TRANSACTION UNDO); only objects that are Modify()'d record (set_editor_property, editor subsystems, obj.modify() first): direct setters such as set_actor_location are neither undoable nor marked unsaved. Engine warnings and errors raised while it runs are returned as logs too. An endless pure-Python loop or runaway recursion does not freeze the editor: it is stopped with a Timeout error after 'timeout' seconds (default 30, capped below the tool timeout) and the editor keeps working. A snippet waiting in join(), time.sleep() or an Event / Queue / Future wait is stopped the same way. One long call into C (an unreal call, a lock acquire, queue.SimpleQueue) finishes first and the run is then a Timeout too. sys.setrecursionlimit is capped at 3000. Threads the snippet starts with threading.Thread are stopped at the budget or once the run ends (when their own Python code runs; not threads blocked in a C call, nor _thread.start_new_thread) and an unfired threading.Timer is cancelled: join the work you start. Known engine crashes that take the editor down (avoid them): importing a malformed or truncated OBJ through Interchange (AssetTools.import_asset_tasks / AssetImportTask) - check the file before importing it; constructing unreal.NiagaraPythonEmitter() directly - read emitters with rql-query (NiagaraSystem.Emitters, Niagara extension). Do not call this editor's MCP server over HTTP from a snippet: that tool call needs the game thread the snippet holds and only times out. Output is capped (~20k characters each for the value and the logs). 'include': helper files/folders (relative to <Project>/.ai-game-dev/snippets): folders are importable, files run before the code. Blueprint graph wiring is not available from Python: add nodes and connect pins with rql-mutate (unreal.asset(path).EventGraph | call AddEvent / AddCallFunction, node | call Connect).

include.description: Helper .py files or folders, relative to <Project>/.ai-game-dev/snippets or absolute.

timeout.description: Time budget in seconds, default 30: a snippet still running then is stopped with a Timeout error. Capped a few seconds below the tool timeout. Use a small value (e.g. 5) to try code that might not end.

name: python-execute
title: Execute Python

description:
Change the live Unreal Editor with an RQL query whose last stage is set or call. All-or-nothing: every target and value is checked before anything is written; a failure changes nothing. One undo step in the editor (Ctrl+Z). Changes are not saved to disk: when the user wants them saved, run editor | call SaveAsset("/Game/Path") (one asset), SaveLevel() or SaveAll(). dry_run=true returns the receipt ($ref, member, old, new) without changing anything. The receipt lists the assignments that change a value; those that keep the old value are only counted (N unchanged). Do exactly the change requested; a read-only member fails with readonly-member instead of being approximated.
  set path = expr, ...   assign members (paths may go through structs: set Location.Z = Location.Z + 100)
                         values see each target: $ (the target), $index (its position in the stream entering set / call), $count (how many enter)
  call Method(args)      invoke a method the tools expose
                         installed extensions add sources with operations (e.g. landscapes, Control Rig, Niagara, PCG,
                         Enhanced Input): check rql-schema before writing C++ or Python for an editor feature
Examples:
  actors | where Label == "Player" | set Location = "(0, 0, 100)"
  actors | get Components | where $ is PointLightComponent | set Intensity = Intensity * 2, LightColor = "#ffcc88"
  actors | where Label starts-with "Coin" | set Scale = Scale * 1.5, Location = Location + [0, 0, 50]       vectors compute component-wise
  actors | where Label starts-with "Enemy" | set bHidden = true          invisible in game (Actor Hidden In Game); HiddenInEditor only hides it in the editor viewport
  actors | where Label starts-with "Pillar_" | set Label = Label.replace("Pillar_", "Column_")      bulk rename
  actors | where Label starts-with "Crate" | sort Label | set Location.X = $index * 200              spread along X
  actors | where Label starts-with "Guard" | set Location = Location + normalize([1, 1, 0]) * 300     3 m diagonally (vector functions: length, normalize, distance, dot, lerp; [X, 0, Z] * k)
  actors | where Label starts-with "Lamp" | set Location = [500 * cos(2 * pi() * $index / $count), 500 * sin(2 * pi() * $index / $count), 300]     a 5 m circle (radians)
  unreal.asset("/Game/Input/IA_Jump") | set Triggers = [{$type: "InputTriggerHold", HoldTimeThreshold: 0.5}], Modifiers = append(Modifiers, {$type: "InputModifierNegate"})
                         instanced subobjects (EditInlineNew: input triggers / modifiers ...) are built from a typed literal for the object that owns them
  actors | get Components | where $ is LightComponentBase | set Intensity = (Intensity > 5000 ? 5000 : Intensity)    clamp
  ref("Button#34") | set Slot.LayoutData.Anchors = "(Minimum=(X=0.5,Y=0),Maximum=(X=0.5,Y=0))"   structs also take UE's text form (the editor's Copy)
  unreal.asset("/Game/Materials/MI_Red") | set Scalars["Roughness"] = 0.2, Vectors["BaseColor"] = "(1, 0, 0, 1)"
Create / add / remove (call; the receipt's result column holds the new object's $ref for follow-up queries):
  editor | call SpawnActor("PointLight", "Lamp", "(0, 0, 300)")          class, label, location (cm: 1 m = 100), rotation, parent, scale
  editor | call SpawnActorFromAsset("/Game/Props/SM_Rock", "Rock", [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0], null, [2, 2, 2])     place an asset (mesh, Blueprint, sound) as drag and drop does
  range(0, 300) | call editor.SpawnActor("/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube", "Cube_" + $, [($ % 20) * 150, floor($ / 20) * 150, 50])   with max_targets=300: a 20 x 15 grid, one undo step
  [["Lamp_A", 0], ["Lamp_B", 400]] | call editor.SpawnActor("PointLight", $[0], [$[1], 0, 300])      one spawn per list entry
  range(0, 10) | call editor.SpawnActor({ClassName: "PointLight", Label: "Lamp_" + $, Location: [$ * 300, 0, 300]})   arguments by name (ClassName Label Location Rotation Parent Scale)
  actors | where Label == "Crate" | call AddComponent("StaticMeshComponent", "Mesh")
  actors | where Label == "Old" | call Destroy()                         components: get Components | where $ is X | call Destroy()
  actors | where Label == "Lamp" | set Parent = ref("StaticMeshActor#1234")   attach, keeping the world transform; null detaches
  actors | where Label == "Crate" | call Duplicate("(200, 0, 0)")        copy with an offset (returns the copy)
Levels, assets, editor state:
  editor | call OpenLevel("/Game/Maps/Arena")        editor | call NewLevel("/Game/Maps/New")
  editor | call SaveLevel()        editor | call SaveAll()        levels | where Map == "Sub" | set IsCurrent = true
  editor | call CreateMaterialInstance("/Game/Materials/MI_Glow", "/Game/Materials/M_Base")
  editor | call CreateAsset("/Game/Data/DA_Sword", "WeaponData")         any asset class (the editor's factory when it has one)
  editor | call CopyAsset("/Game/A", "/Game/B")    MoveAsset / DeleteAsset / CreateFolder("/Game/Props") / ImportAsset("C:/art/crate.fbx", "/Game/Props")   (returns the mesh and the materials / textures it created)
  actors | where Label == "NavBounds" | set BrushExtent = "(2000, 2000, 500)"     a volume's box brush (half-size, cm)
  editor | set Selection = [ref("StaticMeshActor#1234")]        actors | where $ is PointLight | set Selected = true        editor | set IsPlaying = true
Data, tags, settings (settings are saved to their ini at once, tag edits too; neither is undoable):
  unreal.asset("/Game/Data/DT_Weapons") | set Rows["Sword"].Damage = 12        call AddRow("Bow", {Damage: 7}) / RemoveRow / RenameRow / DuplicateRow
  unreal.asset("/Game/Data/DT_Weapons") | get Rows | where Value.Damage > 10 | set Value.Damage = Value.Damage * 2     rows (map entries) as targets
  editor | call CreateDataTable("/Game/Data/DT_Weapons", "WeaponRow")      editor | call AddGameplayTag("Ability.Fire", "fire ability")
  editor | call CreateAsset("/Game/Data/S_Enemy", "UserDefinedStruct")      unreal.asset("/Game/Data/S_Enemy") | call AddField("Health", "float", 100)   RemoveField / RenameField / SetFieldDefault
  unreal.settings("Maps & Modes") | set GameDefaultMap = "/Game/Maps/Arena"
Blueprints (component defaults reach placed actors that keep the old value; each graph Add* returns the node; connect by pin name; Compile returns errors with the node's $ref):
  unreal.asset("/Game/BP_Coin").Components | where Name == "Mesh" | set StaticMesh = "/Engine/BasicShapes/Sphere"
  unreal.asset("/Game/BP_Door").EventGraph | call AddEvent("BeginPlay")      AddCallFunction("PrintString") / AddVariableGet("Health") / AddVariableGet("BP_Player.Score") (Target pin) / AddInputKey("SpaceBar") / AddNode("Branch")
  ref("K2Node_Event#12") | call Connect("then", ref("K2Node_CallFunction#34"), "execute")     ref("K2Node_CallFunction#34") | call SetPinDefault("InString", "Hi")
  unreal.asset("/Game/BP_Door") | call Compile()
Widgets and sequences:
  unreal.asset("/Game/UI/WBP_Menu") | call AddWidget("Button", "Play", ref("VerticalBox#56"))      ref("TextBlock#78") | set Text = "Play"
  unreal.asset("/Game/Cine/LS_Intro") | call AddActor(unreal.find("Door"))      ... | get Bindings | where Name == "Door" | call AddTrack("Transform")
  unreal.asset("/Game/Cine/LS_Intro") | get Bindings | get Tracks | get Sections | call AddKey("Location.Z", 30, 200)    channels: Location.X, Rotation.Yaw, Scale.Z ...
  ... | get Bindings | where Name == "Lamp" | call AddTrack("Intensity")      any animatable property (the light component's too); key it: AddKey("Intensity", 60, 5000)
Object literals build values: set Settings = {Speed: 2}, and instanced subobjects (EditInlineNew classes such as input triggers and modifiers) from a typed literal: {$type: "InputTriggerHold", HoldTimeThreshold: 0.5}, owned by the object written to. Actors, components and assets are never built from literals: reference them (unreal.find("Label"), ref("Type#id"), an asset path) and create them with editor | call SpawnActor / AddComponent / CreateAsset. Destructive cleanup (Destroy, DeleteAsset, removing many items): first list what would go (rql-query, or dry_run=true) and show it to the user; delete only in a second call after that. At most 200 targets per call by default: pass max_targets (up to 1000) for a bigger edit, it stays one all-or-nothing undo step; beyond 1000 split it with first N / skip N. A misspelt member in where / get that leaves set / call nothing to change is an error (nothing changed); a real member no remaining item has is a no-match (0 changes, warning). Filter before setting a member only some classes have: where $ is LightComponentBase (or has(Intensity)) | set Intensity = ... When you use a different member than the user named (a misspelling, or the did-you-mean of a warning), or a different actor / asset than the name the user gave, tell the user which one you changed. Bulk create: range(0, N) | call editor.SpawnActor(... $ ...) spawns N actors in one call (each counts against max_targets; every spawn is checked before the first); the receipt has one row per actor with its $ref.

Query part: the RQL of rql-query (full guide and the sources in its description); unreal.assets("Material"), unreal.asset(path), unreal.find("Label"), ref("PointLight#1234"). Stages: where, select, sort, first N, get <path>, recurse Children. Operators: == != < > and or not, contains, starts-with, $ is PointLight, cond ? a : b; conditions must be booleans (StaticMesh != null, has(x)). Paths a.b.c, list[0], map["key"]. Vectors/colors as "(1, 2, 3)" or "#ff8800"; enums as strings.

Language rules:
- Conditions are booleans. where, and / or / not, ?: and the predicates of .any() .all() .count() .first() take a comparison or has(), never a bare value: where material != null (or has(material)), where count > 0, where name != "", where len(tags) > 0. A number, string, object or list there fails with type-mismatch; null counts as false.
- cond ? a : b (the same as if(cond, a, b)) picks a value and evaluates only the taken branch: set y = (y < 0 ? 0 : y). Inside select, wrap computed values in parentheses: select kind = (intensity > 2 ? "bright" : "dim").
- Lists compare by value, in order: tags == ["a", "b"], x in [[1, 2], [3, 4]]; distinct and group-by merge equal lists.
- group-by gives rows with key (or one column per key), count and the group's items: group-by kind | select key, count, avg = items.avg(weight); also items.sum(e), items.min(e), items.max(e), items.count(pred), items.first().name. Group by the item's type with $type (group-by $type); a bare type is a member that most items do not have.
- Receipts list only real changes: a set row whose value stayed the same is left out and counted as unchanged, so no rows with N unchanged means the values already matched.
- call Method(args) runs the method of each item (the items must be objects). call source.Method(args) runs the method of that one source object once per stream item, with $, $index, $path and $depth in the arguments being the item's; every call counts against the target limit, and every argument is checked before the first call (a dry run checks without calling).
- Bulk create: range(start, end[, step]) streams numbers (end excluded), and a list literal streams its elements, so one call creates many objects: range(0, 150) | call editor.SpawnActor("/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube", "Tile_" + $, [($ % 15) * 200, floor($ / 15) * 200, 0]) builds a 15-wide grid, [["Lamp_A", [0, 0, 300]], ["Lamp_B", [400, 0, 300]]] | call editor.SpawnActor("PointLight", $[0], $[1]) one object per entry. The receipt has one row per call with the $ref of the created object.
- Vectors and colors the host marks as component-wise compute component by component: set Scale = Scale * 1.5, Position + [0, 1, 0], Position - Offset, -Velocity, v / 2. Adding a number to a vector is a type-mismatch (add [x, y, z] instead); quaternions and other types without that mark stay type-mismatch. Lists of numbers are vectors too: [x, 0, z] * k, [1, 2] + [3, 4]. Vector functions work on both: length(v) (or v.length(), magnitude), normalize(v), distance(a, b), dot(a, b), lerp(a, b, t); len(x) stays the size of a string or list.
- Trigonometry is in radians: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2(y, x), pi(), deg(x), rad(x); trigonometric results are rounded (sin(pi()) is 0). In a set value or call argument $count is the number of items entering the stage ($index runs 0 to $count - 1), so set position = [5 * cos(2 * pi() * $index / $count), 0, 5 * sin(2 * pi() * $index / $count)] lays the items out on a circle of radius 5.
- A missing map entry reads as null: props["k"] == null and props["k"] is null are true without the entry, and has(props["k"]) tests whether it exists. A misspelt member is not null: it stays unknown and is reported.
- Arguments by name: call Method({name: value, ...}) with one object literal that no overload takes as a whole binds each key to the parameter of that name; parameters left out keep their defaults, and an unknown name fails listing the parameters: range(0, 10) | call editor.SpawnActor({ClassName: "/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube", Label: "Tile_" + $, Location: [$ * 200, 0, 0]}). Engine objects (scene objects, nodes, actors) are never built from an object literal: pass an existing one, e.g. ref("Type#id"). Value-like assets and owned subobjects that the host marks are built from a typed literal: set mesh = {$type: "TypeName", size: 2}.

dry_run.description: true = preview the receipt without changing anything

max_targets.description: Most objects set / call may change in this call (default 200, at most 1000); raise it for a bigger bulk edit

query.description: RQL query ending with a set or call stage, e.g. actors | where Label == "Player" | set HiddenInEditor = true

name: rql-mutate
title: RQL / Mutate

description:
Run a read-only RQL query against the live Unreal Editor world and return compact rows. One precise query beats many exploratory calls. Changes need rql-mutate.

RQL: source | stage | stage ...
Sources: actors (every actor of the editor world's loaded levels), levels, world, selection, console (editor log entries), editor (editor state and operations), dataTables, gameplayTags, settings (Project Settings / Editor Preferences sections), blueprints, widgetBlueprints, levelSequences, plus the sources of installed extensions (rql-schema lists them). Assets: unreal.assets("Material") or unreal.assets("StaticMesh", "/Game/Props") (at most 200, loaded lazily), unreal.asset("/Game/Materials/M_Red"). ref("PointLight#1234") resolves a $ref; unreal.find("Lamp") an actor by label, name or path; unreal.classes("ActorComponent", "Light") lists classes; unreal.settings("Maps & Modes") a settings object. A member path may follow a function: unreal.asset("/Game/BP_Door").EventGraph.
Stages:
  where <predicate>                  filter
  select a b.c alias=(expr)          project columns (wrap computed expressions in parentheses)
  sort <expr> [desc], ...            stable sort
  first N | skip N | count
  get <path>                         replace each item by a member (lists are flattened)
  recurse Children [max-depth=N] [include-self=false]   walk a hierarchy (input items included by default)
  distinct [expr] | sum expr | min expr | max expr | avg expr
  group-by expr                      rows key|count; group-by a, b (or kind=$type) gives one column per key, then count; aggregate each group's items: group-by $type | select key, count, avg = items.avg(Intensity) (items.sum / .min / .max / .count(pred) / .first().Label)
Expressions: == != < <= > >= and or not + - * / %; contains, starts-with, ends-with, matches "regex" (all case-insensitive); x in [a, b]; x is null; x is not null; $ is PointLight (includes subclasses; a Blueprint's $type is BP_Door_C, $ is BP_Door matches it and its child Blueprints); has(member); functions abs round floor ceil sqrt pow min(a, b) max(a, b) len lower upper coalesce; conditional: cond ? a : b or if(cond, a, b); text: replace(s, from, to) (case-insensitive), replace-regex(s, pattern, repl) ($1 = group 1), substring(s, start[, length]), split(s, sep), trim(s), pad(v, width[, fill]) - also as methods: Label.replace("Old", "New"), Label.substring(0, 4), Index.pad(3). After select, sort / where use the column names (sort Owner.Label). Literals: numbers, "strings", true/false/null, lists [a, b], objects {X: 1, Y: 2}.
Paths: a.b.c, list[0], map["key"]; .member on a list maps over its elements. List methods: .any(pred) .all(pred) .count([pred]) .sum(e) .min(e) .max(e) .first([pred]); inside them bare names refer to the element, falling back to the outer item.
Meta: $ (current item), $ref (stable id such as PointLight#1234), $type, $path, $index, $depth. Enums compare to strings: the entry name, the editor's display name or the number (Mobility == "Movable"); == on strings is case-sensitive.
Unreal: every object has Id, Name, Path. Actor has Label, Location, Rotation, Scale (world transform), Components (list), Children (attached actors), Parent, Folder, Level, HiddenInEditor (editor viewport only), bHidden (Actor Hidden In Game: invisible when playing), Selected; a Volume also BrushExtent (writable: rebuilds its box brush) and BrushBounds. Locations, distances and sizes such as BrushExtent are Unreal units, centimetres, Z up (Scale is a plain multiplier, 1 = original size): a user's metres are x 100 ("start at (-10, -10, 0) m, 2 m apart" is [-1000, -1000, 0] stepping 200). Other members are the reflected properties (UPROPERTY EditAnywhere / VisibleAnywhere / BlueprintVisible) under their C++ names (bHidden, Intensity, RelativeLocation, StaticMesh); find them via actors | get Components | where $ is PointLightComponent (every light: $ is LightComponentBase; LightComponent leaves out sky lights). Vectors, rotators and colors print as (x, y, z) (rotators (pitch, yaw, roll)); write "(1, 2, 3)", [1, 2, 3] or {X: 1, Y: 2, Z: 3}; colors also "#ff8800". Vector, Vector2D, Vector4, LinearColor and Rotator compute component-wise: Scale * 1.5, Location + [0, 0, 100], Location - Other.Location (a rotator per axis, Rotation + [0, 90, 0] adds 90 to Yaw: an editor nudge, not a composed rotation); Quat and Transform do not. Object references accept ref("..."), unreal.asset(path) or an asset path "/Game/Meshes/SM_Cube". Material parameters: Scalars["Roughness"], Vectors["BaseColor"], Textures["Albedo"]. Gameplay tags are text: Tag == "Ability.Fire", set Tags = ["Ability.Fire", "State.Stunned"] (registered tags only). DataTable rows: Rows["Sword"].Damage (RowNames, RowStructName). Blueprints: Components (the components it adds; their defaults: StaticMesh, ...), Graphs / EventGraph -> Nodes -> Pins (Name Direction Type DefaultValue LinkedTo). User-defined structs: Fields. Widget Blueprints: RootWidget / Widgets, panels have Children, widgets Parent, Slot and IsVariable (set true to read the widget in graphs). Level Sequences: Bindings -> Tracks -> Sections -> Channels (frames at the display rate). Destroyed objects read as null (where StaticMesh == null finds empty references). Navigate with paths or get; select only projects output columns.
Results come back as compact rows (header line, then col|col). Long results are truncated - refine with where/first or use count. Unknown members produce warnings with suggestions; rql-schema(type) lists a type's members.
Language rules:
- Conditions are booleans. where, and / or / not, ?: and the predicates of .any() .all() .count() .first() take a comparison or has(), never a bare value: where material != null (or has(material)), where count > 0, where name != "", where len(tags) > 0. A number, string, object or list there fails with type-mismatch; null counts as false.
- cond ? a : b (the same as if(cond, a, b)) picks a value and evaluates only the taken branch: set y = (y < 0 ? 0 : y). Inside select, wrap computed values in parentheses: select kind = (intensity > 2 ? "bright" : "dim").
- Lists compare by value, in order: tags == ["a", "b"], x in [[1, 2], [3, 4]]; distinct and group-by merge equal lists.
- group-by gives rows with key (or one column per key), count and the group's items: group-by kind | select key, count, avg = items.avg(weight); also items.sum(e), items.min(e), items.max(e), items.count(pred), items.first().name. Group by the item's type with $type (group-by $type); a bare type is a member that most items do not have.
- Receipts list only real changes: a set row whose value stayed the same is left out and counted as unchanged, so no rows with N unchanged means the values already matched.
- call Method(args) runs the method of each item (the items must be objects). call source.Method(args) runs the method of that one source object once per stream item, with $, $index, $path and $depth in the arguments being the item's; every call counts against the target limit, and every argument is checked before the first call (a dry run checks without calling).
- Bulk create: range(start, end[, step]) streams numbers (end excluded), and a list literal streams its elements, so one call creates many objects: range(0, 150) | call editor.SpawnActor("/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube", "Tile_" + $, [($ % 15) * 200, floor($ / 15) * 200, 0]) builds a 15-wide grid, [["Lamp_A", [0, 0, 300]], ["Lamp_B", [400, 0, 300]]] | call editor.SpawnActor("PointLight", $[0], $[1]) one object per entry. The receipt has one row per call with the $ref of the created object.
- Vectors and colors the host marks as component-wise compute component by component: set Scale = Scale * 1.5, Position + [0, 1, 0], Position - Offset, -Velocity, v / 2. Adding a number to a vector is a type-mismatch (add [x, y, z] instead); quaternions and other types without that mark stay type-mismatch. Lists of numbers are vectors too: [x, 0, z] * k, [1, 2] + [3, 4]. Vector functions work on both: length(v) (or v.length(), magnitude), normalize(v), distance(a, b), dot(a, b), lerp(a, b, t); len(x) stays the size of a string or list.
- Trigonometry is in radians: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2(y, x), pi(), deg(x), rad(x); trigonometric results are rounded (sin(pi()) is 0). In a set value or call argument $count is the number of items entering the stage ($index runs 0 to $count - 1), so set position = [5 * cos(2 * pi() * $index / $count), 0, 5 * sin(2 * pi() * $index / $count)] lays the items out on a circle of radius 5.
- A missing map entry reads as null: props["k"] == null and props["k"] is null are true without the entry, and has(props["k"]) tests whether it exists. A misspelt member is not null: it stays unknown and is reported.
- Arguments by name: call Method({name: value, ...}) with one object literal that no overload takes as a whole binds each key to the parameter of that name; parameters left out keep their defaults, and an unknown name fails listing the parameters: range(0, 10) | call editor.SpawnActor({ClassName: "/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube", Label: "Tile_" + $, Location: [$ * 200, 0, 0]}). Engine objects (scene objects, nodes, actors) are never built from an object literal: pass an existing one, e.g. ref("Type#id"). Value-like assets and owned subobjects that the host marks are built from a typed literal: set mesh = {$type: "TypeName", size: 2}.

Examples:
  actors | where Label contains "Enemy" | select $ref Label Location
  actors | get Components | where $ is PointLightComponent and Intensity > 2 | select Owner.Label Intensity LightColor
  actors | get Components | where $ is LightComponentBase and CastShadows | sort Intensity desc | select Owner.Label $type Intensity      every light kind (sky lights too)
  actors | where Parent == null | recurse Children | select $depth Label
  actors | where $ is PointLight and distance(Location, unreal.find("Player").Location) < 1000 | select Label      within 10 m (cm)
  unreal.assets("MaterialInstanceConstant") | select Name Scalars Vectors
  console | where Verbosity == "Error" | sort Sequence desc | first 5 | select Message
  actors | get Components | where $ is LightComponentBase | group-by $type | select key, count, avg = items.avg(Intensity)
  levels | select Map IsPersistent IsCurrent IsVisible
  editor | select IsPlaying IsPaused Selection
  editor | select NextUndo UndoHistory RedoHistory      what Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y would revert (RQL steps are "RQL: <query>")
  actors | where $ is Volume | select Label BrushExtent BrushBounds      volume shapes (BrushExtent null = no brush, no shape)
  unreal.asset("/Game/Data/DT_Weapons") | get Rows | where Value.Damage > 10 | select Key Value.Damage
  gameplayTags | where Name starts-with "Ability." | select Name Comment
  settings | where Container == "Project" | select Category Section DisplayName
  unreal.asset("/Game/BP_Door").EventGraph | get Nodes | select $ref Title Pins.Name

query.description: RQL query, e.g. actors | where $ is PointLight | select $ref Label Location

name: rql-query
title: RQL / Query

description: Without a type: RQL sources, functions, and the actor and component classes in the editor world (with counts), plus the Actor members. With a type name (e.g. "PointLight", "StaticMeshComponent", "Vector"): that type's members (name type; ro = read-only) and methods. Use it before querying an unfamiliar class.
name: rql-schema
title: RQL / Schema

description: Render the scene from a chosen camera actor (resolved by label/name/path) and capture it. Returns a base64 PNG as MCP image content. Optional 'width'/'height' are clamped to [1, 2048] per side; the default is 1024. Requires a GPU-backed (windowed) editor.

camera.description: Camera actor reference (label, object name, or path) to render from.

fov.description: Optional horizontal field-of-view override in degrees (clamped to [5, 170]); defaults to the camera component's FOV (or 90).

height.description: Optional output height in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); default 1024.

width.description: Optional output width in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); default 1024.

name: screenshot-camera
title: Screenshot Camera

description: Capture the Play-In-Editor game view. Errors when no PIE session is active. Returns a base64 PNG as MCP image content. Optional 'width'/'height' are clamped to [1, 2048] per side; the default is 1024. Requires a GPU-backed (windowed) editor.

height.description: Optional output height in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); when only 'width' is given the height is derived from the native aspect ratio, and the native game-view height is used when both are omitted.

width.description: Optional output width in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); when only 'height' is given the width is derived from the native aspect ratio, and the native game-view width is used when both are omitted.

name: screenshot-game-view
title: Screenshot Game View

description: Render a single actor in isolation against a neutral background, auto-framed by its bounds. Returns a base64 PNG as MCP image content. Optional 'width'/'height' are clamped to [1, 2048] per side; the default is 1024. Requires a GPU-backed (windowed) editor.

actor.description: Target actor reference (label, object name, or path) to render in isolation.

background.description: Optional background color as hex ('#RRGGBB' or '#RRGGBBAA'); the alpha of '#RRGGBBAA' is accepted but ignored (the PNG is always opaque). Defaults to dark grey.

fov.description: Optional field-of-view override in degrees (clamped to [5, 170]); default 50.

height.description: Optional output height in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); default 1024.

width.description: Optional output width in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); default 1024.

name: screenshot-isolated
title: Screenshot Isolated Actor

description: Capture the active editor viewport. Note: while a Play-In-Editor session has viewport focus the 'active viewport' is the PIE game view; use screenshot-game-view to capture the game view explicitly. Returns a base64 PNG as MCP image content. Optional 'width'/'height' are clamped to [1, 2048] per side; the default is 1024. Requires a GPU-backed (windowed) editor.

height.description: Optional output height in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); when only 'width' is given the height is derived from the native aspect ratio, and the native viewport height is used when both are omitted.

width.description: Optional output width in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); when only 'height' is given the width is derived from the native aspect ratio, and the native viewport width is used when both are omitted.

name: screenshot-viewport
title: Screenshot Viewport

description: Compile the project's C++ and return a STRUCTURED diagnostic report — the AI feedback loop. Prefers Live Coding when the editor is interactive and Live Coding is active, otherwise invokes UnrealBuildTool on the project's Editor target ('target' overrides; default '<Project>Editor'). The result carries 'diagnostics' (an array of {file,line,severity,message}), 'errorCount'/'warningCount', the process 'returnCode', 'success' (returnCode==0) and 'compileClean' (zero compiler errors — true even when a running editor holds the module DLL so the link stage cannot relink it). Set 'useLiveCoding':false to force the UBT path.

platform.description: Build platform. Default the host platform (e.g. 'Win64').

useLiveCoding.description: Prefer Live Coding when available (interactive editor only). Default true.

name: source-compile
title: Compile Project C++

description: Scaffold a new C++ class — header + cpp generated from templates into Source/<module>/, mirroring the editor's 'New C++ Class'. 'className' is the bare name WITHOUT the U/A/F prefix (the prefix is derived from the parent). 'parentClass' is one of: UObject (default), Actor, ActorComponent, None (a plain non-UCLASS class). 'module' defaults to the project's primary module. Refuses to overwrite existing files unless 'force':true. All writes are JAILED to <Project>/Source.

className.description: Bare class name (no U/A/F prefix), e.g. 'MyActor'.

force.description: Overwrite existing header/cpp at the destination. Default false.

module.description: Target module folder under Source/. Defaults to the project's primary module.

parentClass.description: Parent kind: UObject (default), Actor, ActorComponent, or None.

name: source-create-class
title: Create C++ Class

description: Delete a source file. JAILED to <Project>/Source — refuses directories and any path outside the jail. Destructive and not undoable from MCP.

path.description: Source file path relative to <Project>/Source (or absolute, inside it).

name: source-delete
title: Delete Source File

description: Enumerate source files with their byte sizes. Scoped to 'module' (a folder under Source/) when given, else the whole <Project>/Source tree. 'recursive' (default true) walks sub-folders. By default lists .h/.cpp/.cs; pass 'extensions' (array of extensions without the dot) to override. JAILED to <Project>/Source.

extensions.description: Extensions to include (without the dot). Default ['h','cpp','cs'].

module.description: Module folder under Source/ to scope the listing. Omit for the whole tree.

name: source-list
title: List Source Files

description: Read a project C++/C# source file. 'path' is relative to the project Source/ directory (e.g. 'MyGame/MyActor.cpp') or an absolute path inside it; all access is JAILED to <Project>/Source. Optionally window the result by 1-based 'startLine'/'endLine' (inclusive). The returned text is byte-capped by 'maxBytes' (default 262144, hard cap 4194304); 'truncated' reports whether the cap clipped it.

endLine.description: 1-based last line to return (inclusive). Default: end of file.

maxBytes.description: Maximum bytes of content to return (1..4194304). Default 262144.

path.description: Source file path relative to <Project>/Source (or absolute, inside it).

name: source-read
title: Read Source File

description: Replace an existing source file's full contents, or a 1-based inclusive line range. Pass 'content' (the replacement text). Omit 'startLine'/'endLine' to replace the whole file; pass both to splice 'content' over that line range. The file must already exist (use source-create-class for new files). JAILED to <Project>/Source.

path.description: Source file path relative to <Project>/Source (or absolute, inside it).

name: source-update
title: Update Source File

description: List every tool of this Unreal Editor, including the ones hidden from tools/list (marked hidden): a hidden tool still runs when called by name. Optional regex 'filter' on the name, title and description; 'includeDescription' / 'includeInputs' add each tool's description and parameters.

filter.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against each tool's name, title and description.

includeDescription.description: Add each tool's full description (default false).

includeInputs.description: Add each tool's parameters as name: type (default false).

name: unreal-tool-list
title: List Tools

content.text:
sources:
  gameplayTags: list of GameplayTagInfo — every registered gameplay tag, sorted (Name, Comment, Source ini, Parent, Children, Explicit, Restricted); change the list with editor | call AddGameplayTag / RemoveGameplayTag / RenameGameplayTag
  dataTables: list of DataTable — the project's DataTables (Rows by name, RowNames, RowCount, RowStructName; call AddRow / RemoveRow / RenameRow / DuplicateRow)
  settings: list of SettingsSection — the sections of Project Settings (Container "Project") and Editor Preferences ("Editor"): Container Category Section DisplayName Description, Object = the settings object; writes to its config properties are saved to its ini at once (not undoable)
  blueprints: list of Blueprint — the project's Blueprints (Components, Graphs, EventGraph, Status; call Compile / AddFunction); graphs list Nodes, nodes list Pins
  widgetBlueprints: list of BaseWidgetBlueprint — the project's Widget Blueprints (RootWidget, Widgets; call AddWidget / Compile); panels list Children, widgets have Parent and Slot
  levelSequences: list of LevelSequence — the project's Level Sequences (DisplayRate Start End Bindings Tracks; call AddActor / AddTrack); sections have Start End Channels, call AddKey
  actors: list of Actor — every actor of the editor world's loaded levels (hidden ones included)
  levels: list of Level — the loaded levels of the editor world (Map, IsPersistent, IsCurrent, IsVisible, Actors)
  world: World — the editor world (Levels, PersistentLevel, CurrentLevel)
  selection: list of Actor — the actors selected in the editor (write it: editor | set Selection = [...])
  editor: Editor — editor state (IsPlaying, IsPaused, Selection, World, CurrentLevel, NextUndo / UndoHistory / RedoHistory) and operations: call SpawnActor / SpawnActorFromAsset / OpenLevel / NewLevel / SaveLevel / SaveAll / AddSublevel / UnloadSublevel / CreateAsset / CopyAsset / MoveAsset / DeleteAsset / CreateFolder / RefreshAssets / CreateMaterialInstance / ImportAsset / SaveAsset / ClearConsole / CreateDataTable / AddGameplayTag / RemoveGameplayTag / RenameGameplayTag
  console: list of LogEntry — editor log entries captured since startup, oldest first (Sequence, Time, Verbosity, Category, Message)
functions:
  unreal.asset(…) — the asset at a path ("/Game/Materials/M_Red"), loaded; null when there is none
  unreal.assets(…) — assets of a class ("Material", "StaticMesh", "Blueprint") under a content path (default /Game), at most 200, loaded as the query reads them
  unreal.classes(…) — classes deriving from a base (default "Actor") whose name contains a filter: Name Path Parent Abstract Blueprint (at most 500)
  unreal.find(…) — the actor with this label, name or path in the editor world
  unreal.settings(…) — the settings object of a Project Settings / Editor Preferences section by name ("Maps & Modes", "GameMapsSettings", "Input"); writes are saved to its ini
actor classes in the editor world: AbstractNavData ×1, Actor ×1, Brush ×1, BuoyancyManager ×1, DefaultPhysicsVolume ×1, GameplayDebuggerPlayerManager ×1, PlayerStart ×1, WorldSettings ×1
component classes in the editor world: BillboardComponent ×3, BrushComponent ×2, ArrowComponent ×1, CapsuleComponent ×1, ChaosDebugDrawComponent ×1, InputComponent ×1, SceneComponent ×1
